infosec.summary: Besxar, a $9.35 million seed-funded startup, flew its first mission on July 5 aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 alongside a Starlink batch, carrying its own semiconductor wafers plus test wafers from the University of Virginia and UT Austin. The company's pitch is simple: Earth-based fabs spend billions on pumps to create the vacuum semiconductors need, but in space vacuum is free, so Besxar wants to manufacture higher-quality, lower-cost wafers in orbit and return them to Earth to sell.

infosec.title: vLLM triples MiniMax M3 inference throughput on AMD's MI355X through systematic bottleneck chasing
infosec.summary: AMD and Embedded LLM teams took MiniMax M3's day-0 vLLM implementation from 109.1 to 342.4 output tokens/s/GPU on AMD's Instinct MI355X, a 3.14x gain, by repeatedly asking five questions as the bottleneck kept shifting: what local shape reached each rank after tensor-parallel sharding, what work repeats every layer, which bytes actually move, whether a claimed fast path actually executed, and which queue grows once kernels stop being the limiter. Big wins came from fusing the model's shared expert into the same grouped GEMMs as routed experts (up to 30% faster at low concurrency), and reusing sparse-attention block selections across adjacent layers instead of recomputing per layer.

infosec.title: LG denies claims its smart TVs constantly record and upload audio
infosec.summary: Gamers Nexus published a two-hour investigation, done with security researchers MrBruh and uturn using packet capture and firmware analysis, alleging LG's smart TVs constantly log and upload user data even offline or in standby, scan local Wi-Fi networks for other devices, and record and store ambient audio through the TV's microphone for later retrieval, even when the TV appears off. LG called the claims untrue, saying its TVs only process voice data when the remote's voice button is pressed or its "Hi LG" wake word is detected after a user manually enables far-field voice recognition, with wake-word audio processed entirely on-device and deleted immediately if no match is found.

design.title: Shopify Acquires Tailwind
design.summary: Shopify is acquiring Tailwind Labs, bringing the team behind Tailwind CSS, installed more than 110 million times a week by firms like OpenAI and Cloudflare, in-house. The framework stays open source and MIT-licensed, with Tailwind's creator Adam Wathan citing a stable long-term home for millions of dependent developers as the goal. The deal follows layoffs of three of four engineers in January after revenue fell 80%, and leaves Tailwind Labs closing sign-ups for commercial products like Tailwind Plus.

design.title: OpenAI's ChatGPT Images Gets Faster, with Sharper Details and More Refined Edits
design.summary: OpenAI's ChatGPT Images 2.5 generates images up to 50% faster, with more natural lighting, richer textures, and steadier detail preservation across edits and long conversations. A new Sketch tool lets users draw a rough reference for the model to build on, while the Flare and Sunburst variants weigh speed against fidelity. The model, rolling out now in ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex plus API access, also adds guardrails, C2PA metadata, and watermarking to flag AI-generated content.

design.title: iPhone 18 Pro officially announced: Here's what's new
design.summary: Apple has unveiled the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max with the new A20 Pro chip, a smaller Dynamic Island, improved battery life, a 48MP variable-aperture camera with expanded manual controls, and AI-focused enhancements powered by a 32-core Neural Engine. Other highlights include faster graphics, better thermal management, support for Apple Reference Image authenticity metadata, up to 2TB of storage, and new accessories, with preorders opening September 12 and devices launching September 18.

design.title: The iPhone Duo is perfect for people with uncanny alien fingers
design.summary: Apple's marketing for the new $1,999 foldable iPhone Duo has drawn criticism after promotional images appeared to use unrealistically long fingers to make the device seem easier to hold one-handed. The exaggerated visuals sparked jokes and accusations of misleading marketing, adding to the debate over the Duo's ergonomics alongside its price and unconventional design.

design.title: How I Design with AI
design.summary: Product design with AI turns to slop unless constraints come first and the extra copy, lines, and icons agents love to add get removed. The approach favors iterating in a design tool like Figma rather than the codebase, building reusable component libraries, and validating results with preview deploys against real data. At Ref, the team also borrows interface patterns from existing products for context and stress-tests taste by critiquing drafts as a group until something holds up.

design.title: Designers Should Be Paid the Same as Engineers
design.summary: Designers who design and ship, not just hand off files, deserve engineering-level pay, since compensation has long tracked who ships work rather than who shapes it. Levels.fyi data puts median product-designer pay near $170,000 against $226,000 for engineers, with designer compensation growing just 1.8% a year versus faster-compounding engineering salaries. Hybrid design-engineer roles, like one at Ramp spanning $172,000 to $440,000, already pay closer to engineering, and the fix is negotiating a shipped product against that band.

design.title: Your AI Design Engineer
design.summary: Kombai is your AI design engineer for designing standout websites and product UIs, then shipping production-ready frontend in the same loop.

design.title: Explorable Worlds Grown from a Single Picture
design.summary: A series of explorable worlds, each grown from a single picture. Click anything in the frame, choose what happens to it, and AI generates the next scene and a short film of the moment in between.

design.summary: React components for PDF, DOCX, XLSX, and CSV viewers, with bounding box citations, file upload, e-signing, and more.

design.title: 10 Common Logo Design Mistakes That Make Brands Look Unprofessional
design.summary: Ten recurring mistakes make brands look unprofessional, according to a new logo design guide, from skipping brand strategy to cramming too many ideas into one mark. Other flagged missteps include trendy typefaces, unnecessary effects, overly detailed forms, generic stock symbols, and designing only in color instead of testing black-and-white first.

design.title: O0 extends Fauna Robotics' brand into a system that moves on screen
design.summary: O0 evolved Fauna Robotics' existing identity into a flexible digital brand system centered on motion, modularity, and the adaptable nature of its Sprout robot, making the product feel approachable while remaining technically credible. The website combines photography, video, 3D, and interactive storytelling to introduce the robot, explain its capabilities, and build trust through layered technical detail rather than marketing claims. The scalable design system helped position Fauna Robotics for growth ahead of its acquisition by Amazon in March.

design.title: How to Test Interface States AI Agents Usually Miss
design.summary: AI-generated prototypes often look complete in happy-path form while states like loading, empty results, permission changes, and overlapping actions remain undefined. A better process builds a state inventory, embeds those states in realistic tasks and transitions, and measures comprehension and recovery, not just preference, across desktop and mobile. Findings get converted into reusable interface contracts defining triggers, messages, actions, and recovery behavior, so future AI-assisted designs don't reinvent handling for loading, empty, and error states.

marketing.title: AI Overviews may be affecting Shopping ad CTR and impressions
marketing.summary: Shopping ad CTRs are rising while impressions are falling across thousands of campaigns, with clicks relatively flat or slightly down. One hypothesis is that Google's AI Overviews are appearing on queries less likely to generate ad clicks, leaving Shopping ads for higher-intent searches. The data doesn't prove AI Overviews are causing the decline, but advertisers should look beyond CTR and track impressions, clicks, and overall traffic to understand whether performance is actually improving.

marketing.title: YouTube influencers have an AI audience: What millions of citation events reveal about influencer sponsorships
marketing.summary: Sponsored YouTube videos can extend their marketing value into AI search when the video is cited, especially through the description text that names the sponsor. The sponsor appeared in 40% of AI answers that cited a sponsored video, compared with 32.3% when the video was not cited, and the lift reached 1.35x on unbranded prompts. Brands should make specific description language part of influencer contracts and track YouTube citations for the prompts that matter to them, rather than treating sponsorship as a view-based channel alone. The opportunity is temporary because YouTube citation rates fell 43% within a month, so citation monitoring needs to be ongoing.

marketing.title: The Legacy Brand De-Aging Playbook
marketing.summary: Sometimes a brand's old identity becomes valuable again simply because the category around it moved. As dining shifted toward fast casual, delivery, and pricier meals, Chili's leaned into value, booths, and the Triple Dipper, and a format that once looked dated became the countertrend against expensive takeout. Barnes & Noble made a similar bet, handing individual stores control over what to stock and display instead of running every location identically, so each one behaves like a local bookstore again. Both bets worked because the brand stopped trying to outrun its category and let the category's shift make its old strengths relevant.

marketing.title: Don't recommend your most expensive option
marketing.summary: Increase sales by labeling a mid-priced product as “recommended” instead of your most expensive option. In eight experiments involving more than 6,200 participants, sales of a recommended cafe drink increased 58% when a pricier option was added, while sales were unchanged without the recommendation. Consumers appear more receptive to recommendations when the suggested product is cheaper because the brand seems less motivated by profit. Use objective badges such as “Bestseller” when recommending a premium product, and test this pricing tactic on comparable products where customers can easily evaluate the price difference.

marketing.title: The New Rules of Growth: live with Stripe and OpenAI's first marketer
marketing.summary: Krithika S., Stripe and OpenAI's first marketing hire and now head of marketing at Thrive Capital, joins Christy Roach (CMO, AirOps) live on Sep 17. They break down a new study of 300+ marketing teams: how high-growth teams hire, budget, and win more resources. Free, one hour. Save A Spot Now

marketing.title: Google launches tool to check whether ads actually increase sales
marketing.summary: Google released an open-source tool that tests whether an ad actually caused a sale, not just which platform claims credit for one. GeoX works by comparing regions where a campaign keeps running against regions where it's paused or given more budget, then measuring how sales in each group differ from what historical data would have predicted anyway. It can track spend across platforms beyond Google's own and combine online and offline sales in the same test. It plugs into Google's existing Meridian measurement software, so the results can also refine how a budget gets split across channels.

marketing.title: Amazon gives OpenAI's ad business a boost, letting its advertisers into ChatGPT
marketing.summary: Amazon has spent months locking AI shopping agents like Claude and Gemini out of its own storefront while building its own AI shopping tools, then quietly became ChatGPT's top retail advertiser between April and August instead. It's now opening that same access to other brands that already buy through its demand-side platform, letting them run ads inside ChatGPT conversations too. Campaigns are still set up and managed inside Amazon's own systems, while OpenAI's ad system keeps control over which ad actually gets served.

marketing.title: AI, tools and transformation
marketing.summary: AI will not eliminate software so much as change how companies decide what gets automated, standardized, or left improvised. Most employees do not naturally identify the workflows that should become software, and important processes often span multiple teams and systems, so successful automation still requires people who can spot problems, design solutions, and get the organization to adopt them. AI will expand existing software and make tools like spreadsheets, email, and chatbots more capable, while also creating new vertical applications that move work between improvised and institutionalized systems. The bigger opportunity for businesses is to look beyond faster versions of existing workflows and identify new products, services, and operating models that AI makes possible for the first time.

marketing.title: Some companies are using ads to influence AI agents
marketing.summary: Time magazine is testing ads designed specifically for AI agents, exposing them to brand-verified facts before they access webpages. The goal is to influence what AI systems retain and potentially correct inaccurate information about brands. As agentic traffic grows, companies are also optimizing websites and product data for AI discovery and recommendations. Brands are beginning to treat AI agents as an emerging advertising and distribution channel.

marketing.title: How Starface Made Pimple Patches Cool
marketing.summary: Skincare spent decades built around the idea that a good product should be invisible. Starface inverted that by making a pimple patch impossible to miss, then expanded through Target, Walmart, Sephora, and Ulta specifically because its bright yellow stars stand out against a retail aisle of clinical whites and pastels. That same bet is now showing up industry-wide, with LED light masks and other visible skincare wearables replacing creams that disappear on the skin.

founders.title: AI spend per employee slumped at top firms in August — summer doldrums or a warning sign?
founders.summary: Ramp's August card data covers 70,000 companies, and it is the number your board will compare your AI spend against. More than half of companies pay for at least one AI product, but that share barely grew, up 0.4% on July. At the heaviest spenders, spend per employee fell almost 10% to $7,205, and part of that is price. The average cost of a million tokens has dropped to $0.68 from a March peak of $1.15, so the same usage costs less each month. If you sell AI, customers' bills are shrinking without them buying less.

founders.title: Divorced from reality
founders.summary: AI venture markets are pricing early-stage companies as if many could become Anthropic-scale outcomes even as mature software assets sell for modest revenue multiples. That gap is fueling investor anxiety and raising the risk of overpaying for consensus deals.

founders.title: The SaaSpocalypse was more like a RenaiSaaS
founders.summary: SaaS valuations dropped nearly $2 trillion in early 2026 due to fears about AI disrupting business models, but revenue growth quickly rebounded. The Stripe SaaS Index, measuring weekly pay-in volumes of 72,000 non-AI SaaS businesses, showed strong growth post-sell-off, particularly among young companies and in the US market. Healthcare, retail, and professional services sectors outperformed pre-crisis trends, with AI adoption contributing to the resilience, especially among younger firms.

founders.title: The Golden Snitch
founders.summary: Exceptional performance often comes from finding the one outcome that matters more than assigned tasks. Teams should distinguish visible activity from decisive results, give proven employees autonomy, and identify which achievement would materially change the company's trajectory.

founders.title: Ecstatic Highs and Suicidal Lows
founders.summary: Startup leaders face volatile emotional swings when teams fall behind critical milestones. Effective leadership requires adapting to the moment: challenge teams during highs, absorb pressure during lows, remove bottlenecks, and choose tools deliberately instead of amplifying stress by default.

founders.title: An Ode to Counter-Positioning
founders.summary: Counter-positioning allows startups to challenge incumbents by adopting business models that incumbents can't replicate without harming their own profit structures. Examples include Ramp's focus on saving customer money and Base Power's shift from battery sales to electricity services. This strategy buys startups time to develop lasting moats like Scale Economies and Network Effects.

founders.summary: Data agent ChatGPT work can help people answer questions about themselves by connecting company data, investigating what changed, and building interactive, shareable dashboards. Users can direct and refine analysis within conversations without writing queries or learning a new analytics tool. The data agent connects to approved data sources and uses organizations' business terms, metric inhibitions, custom calculations, and data relationships to interpret the data. The context comes from semantic layers and trusted sources.

founders.title: Introducing the Agents API
founders.summary: OpenAI's Agents API is now in public beta. The API brings the same harness and infrastructure that powers Codex to developers through a simple and flexible API. It allows developers to create useful agents with a powerful harness that manages context, uses tools efficiently, and coordinates subagents. The API provides infrastructure to keep agents running reliably for days, and environments where agents can work with files, run code, and save intermediate results.

founders.title: Salesforce Introduces the Trusted Enterprise AI Harness
founders.summary: Salesforce has introduced a new architecture that gives AI a shared understanding of the customer and the business. The new capabilities give AI the ability to act with trust within an open and composable AI ecosystem. The agent understands what is happening, decides what to do next, takes action across systems, and works alongside people and other agents. It brings together what agents need to understand the business, reason and plan, take action, and operate within enterprise controls.

crypto.title: MetaMask Begins Its Next Chapter as an Independent Company
crypto.summary: Consensys Software Inc. is rebranding as MetaMask, consolidating its identity around the consumer wallet product while spinning out its protocols and institutional infrastructure businesses into a separate entity that will carry the Consensys name forward. The split cleanly divides the organization's assets: the MetaMask brand and consumer wallet stay with the newly renamed company, while Linea (the Ethereum L2) and enterprise tooling move to the new Consensys entity. The restructuring gives MetaMask a focused mandate as a standalone consumer product company, freeing it from the overhead of running institutional infrastructure under one roof. For Linea, operating under a dedicated infrastructure-focused parent may accelerate its go-to-market toward developers and institutional integrators without competing internally for resources against a mass-market wallet.

crypto.title: Hunter Biden's LAPTOP airdrops briefly worth over $1 million each before 99% crash
crypto.summary: Hunter Biden airdropped 4,276 LAPTOP tokens on Base to each Substack subscriber enrolled before September 6, with those allocations carrying a theoretical peak value of roughly $1.3M per wallet when the token hit $300 in its first hour. Thin order depth made executing sales near that peak infeasible for most recipients, and the token shed over 99% within minutes, settling near $2. Airdrop recipients who held through the collapse could still redeem approximately $8,000 per wallet, a sharp contrast to the 11,500+ wallets that bought during the run-up, leaving over 80% of those purchasers in the red. Supply is split 10% to community airdrop, 30% to founders under six-month lockups and 24-month vesting schedules, and 30% tied to real-world prediction outcomes that either burn tokens or redirect them to charity.

crypto.title: Coinbase for Agents Now Available on Grok
crypto.summary: Coinbase for Agents is now natively integrated with Grok, letting users connect their Coinbase account at grok.com to execute trades, analyze portfolios, and automate financial workflows without any MCP configuration. Users can sign in with Coinbase, then use Grok to trade across crypto, derivatives, and equities – and eventually anything available on the Coinbase platform.

crypto.title: Introducing the Dolphin Foundation: One Network One Asset
crypto.summary: The Dolphin Foundation has incorporated in the Cayman Islands as the legal entity for Dolphin Network, a decentralized peer-to-pool inference protocol where GPU providers earn POD tokens for completed inference work. POD is the sole value-accruing asset, with 100% of inference revenue from API access and credit card subscriptions directed to open-market POD purchases, creating buy pressure proportional to usage. The structure eliminates the split-incentive problem common in foundation models by removing an equity layer that would otherwise compete with token holders for economic upside. The foundation holds core IP and manages commercial relationships the decentralized protocol cannot, with the inference API launch imminent.

crypto.title: Open Standard: Stablecoins Are Supposed To Be Better Dollars
crypto.summary: Open USD is the structural incentive misalignment in stablecoin design, where issuers earn revenue from idle reserve AUM and are therefore disincentivized to support settlement use cases that reduce those balances. Open Standard's model shares reserve yield proportionally with developers who build on Open USD, replaces burn fees with a small per-transaction fee, and eliminates exit costs when converting to other assets, tying issuer revenue to volume rather than float. Target use cases include card settlement infrastructure for Visa and Mastercard, stablecoin collateral acceptance on institutional venues such as NYSE and CME, and programmatic corporate treasury management via tokenized money market funds. The project has received thousands of partnership inquiries since its summer announcement, signaling substantial institutional appetite for a stablecoin model aligned to transaction throughput.

crypto.title: Why crypto cards cost 2% abroad
crypto.summary: Most issuers settle with Visa/Mastercard in a single currency (usually USD), triggering cross-border assessment fees (~0.13-0.14% baseline, jumping with currency mismatch by up to 0.6%) plus FX spreads (0.1-0.4%), adding over 1% in network costs alone before issuer/program margin. Multi-currency settlement (registering several currencies with the network, the model Revolut/Wise pioneered) and local issuance (issuing cards domestically in each market so transactions never count as cross-border) are two potential workarounds here. Only a few stablecoin issuers like Wirex, StraitsX, and Monavate currently do either. Wirex's EURC settlement volume has grown from zero to ~$500M of Visa's $20B annualized stablecoin volume in a year. Structural and technical constraints (sponsor bank limitations, cost of reissuing card portfolios) explain why most others haven't caught up, though Stripe/Bridge and Rain say wider currency support is on their roadmap.

crypto.title: Could Robinhood stock tokens ever carry voting rights?
crypto.summary: Robinhood's tokenized stocks (structured as debt securities issued by a Jersey entity, backed 1:1 by real shares in US custody) could theoretically let tokenholders direct the underlying shares' proxy votes if Robinhood built an on-chain voting mechanism. This could potentially let a large-enough token holder bloc support board nominees at real public companies, raising concerns about outside/foreign influence over US corporate governance.

crypto.title: EtherFi Cash tax treatment by region
crypto.summary: This thread breaks down how EtherFi Cash's tax treatment varies drastically by country. In the EU and US, "Direct Pay" spending counts as a taxable crypto disposal, while "Borrow Mode" (spending against borrowed funds) generally isn't taxed until repayment/liquidation. The UAE has no personal income or capital gains tax. Kazakhstan taxes disposals around 10%. Onboarding is blocked entirely in India, South Africa, the Netherlands, Estonia, and Finland, and Kenya/Nigeria have their own evolving digital-asset tax frameworks.

crypto.summary: Mastercard launched Wallet Pay, connecting 3.7 billion Mastercard credentials to digital wallets (which have 4.3B users globally, projected to pass 6B by 2030), covering NFC, QR, and online payments.

it.summary: Anthropic Alignment Science Lead Evan Hubinger said he personally believes there is a greater than 10% chance AI could “kill all humans” within the next decade. He added that Anthropic still does not have a clear solution for aligning superintelligent AI, following another researcher's resignation over the pace of development.

it.title: Oracle's cloud infrastructure revenue jumps 121%
it.summary: Oracle's cloud infrastructure revenue grew 121% year over year as demand for AI compute continued to surge. The company spent $28.5 billion on capital expenditures during the quarter and maintained plans for $90–95 billion in spending this fiscal year

it.title: Microsoft goes after Salesforce and ERP users with AI-powered converter
it.summary: Microsoft has launched a public preview of Dynamics 365 Activate, an AI-powered tool to help partners and customers migrate from Salesforce to Dynamics 365 with less manual effort and lower risk. The company says the tool profiles data, relationships, and customizations to create a migration blueprint, and plans additional CRM and ERP migration scenarios later this year.

it.title: The “Left” in Shift-Left Moved
it.summary: AI has shifted left from code repositories to coding agents on developer endpoints with broad privileges, where AppSec has limited control. AI-driven discovery is also flooding defenders with vulnerabilities. The better approach is to eliminate entire vulnerability classes rather than fix tickets one by one, while rethinking human-in-the-loop oversight when agents can both write and remediate code.

it.title: OpenAI board member warns industry isn't ready for loss-of-control risks
it.summary: OpenAI nonprofit board member Paul Christiano says the industry is not currently on track to prevent a potentially catastrophic loss of control over advanced AI. His warning adds to growing concern around how quickly increasingly autonomous systems are being developed.

it.title: Accenture and Google Cloud Deepen Partnership with Formation of New Accenture Gemini Enterprise Business Group
it.summary: Accenture and Google Cloud launched a new Gemini Enterprise group, including a 1,000-person FDE workforce, to scale agentic AI adoption. The group will help enterprises move from AI pilots to production with industry-specific solutions and implementation support. YouTube saw 11% higher customer sentiment and 37% lower handle time using Gemini Enterprise.

it.title: Boost productivity with 5 new agentic AI capabilities

Gemini can create Slides from Chat, build Sheets from Drive, draft and send emails from Docs, turn Gmail threads into structured Docs briefs, and convert Docs into branded decks. The features are rolling out now to Business, Enterprise, Google AI Pro and Ultra, and education plans.

it.title: Big Law starts building its own AI infrastructure
it.summary: Latham & Watkins has bought Nvidia GPU servers and is running customized open-weight models on infrastructure it controls. The move shows large enterprises exploring private AI stacks for greater control over sensitive data, costs, and model choice.

it.title: Modernizing complex legacy code with AI agents
it.summary: Mistral says it helped a European energy operator migrate 40,000 lines of Fortran 77 reservoir-simulator code to C++ using supervised AI-agent workflows. The team built a numerical parity harness first, documented the codebase with over a hundred agents, and found that structured workflows with human review gates beat full autonomy. The first sprint covered core functionality of a 300,000-line system.

it.title: Keycloak vs Ory

it.title: Nvidia and Palantir bring AI to critical supply chains
it.summary: Nvidia is combining Nemotron models with Palantir's platform to automate supply-chain decisions while keeping proprietary enterprise data under tighter control.

hardware.title: OpenAI may double-source next-gen AI chips at Samsung, alongside TSMC
hardware.summary: OpenAI Korea GM Harrison Kim revealed the company has made real progress with Samsung Electronics on joint production and research for its next-generation chips, expanding a relationship that so far has been mostly about memory supply and enterprise software. OpenAI's current inference ASIC, Jalapeño, was designed with Broadcom and built at TSMC in under 18 months and is already in mass production there, so any Samsung involvement more plausibly targets its successor, which is reportedly approaching tapeout.

Apple also unveiled the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max ($1,199/$1,299, up $100 from last year) with new A20 Pro processors, a variable mechanical aperture camera, and 24-30 hour battery life, alongside the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, which add a 5-second heart rate sensor Apple claims is more accurate than a chest strap.

hardware.title: Introducing CUDA Rust for High-Performance GPU Kernel Development
hardware.summary: NVIDIA has announced CUDA Rust and introduced two specialized compilation tracks that allow developers to author and optimize GPU compute kernels directly in Rust. This release brings Rust's strong compile-time memory safety guarantees and modern tooling ecosystem to GPU-accelerated workloads. Developers implementing embedded vision, intensive sensor fusion, and real-time state estimation on mobile platforms can now exploit GPU compute power while minimizing memory-related crashes and runtime concurrency bugs.

hardware.title: TSMC's August revenue jumps 53% to a record high, plans High-NA EUV adoption for 2030
hardware.summary: TSMC posted NT$514.8 billion ($16.1 billion) in August revenue, up 53.3% year-over-year and 10.1% from July, hitting a fresh monthly record as AI-driven chip demand keeps outpacing supply. It came alongside a separate announcement with Dutch equipment maker ASML: TSMC plans to bring ASML's High-NA EUV lithography into large-scale manufacturing starting in 2030 for its most advanced nodes, as AI accelerators push toward increasingly complex transistor architectures.

hardware.title: Besxar flies first suborbital semiconductor manufacturing demo, banking on free vacuum in space
hardware.summary: Besxar, a $9.35 million seed-funded startup, flew its first mission on July 5 aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 alongside a Starlink batch, carrying its own semiconductor wafers plus test wafers from the University of Virginia and UT Austin. The company's pitch is simple: Earth-based fabs spend billions on pumps to create the vacuum semiconductors need, but in space vacuum is free, so Besxar wants to manufacture higher-quality, lower-cost wafers in orbit and return them to Earth to sell.

hardware.title: vLLM triples MiniMax M3 inference throughput on AMD's MI355X through systematic bottleneck chasing
hardware.summary: AMD and Embedded LLM teams took MiniMax M3's day-0 vLLM implementation from 109.1 to 342.4 output tokens/s/GPU on AMD's Instinct MI355X, a 3.14x gain, by repeatedly asking five questions as the bottleneck kept shifting: what local shape reached each rank after tensor-parallel sharding, what work repeats every layer, which bytes actually move, whether a claimed fast path actually executed, and which queue grows once kernels stop being the limiter. Big wins came from fusing the model's shared expert into the same grouped GEMMs as routed experts (up to 30% faster at low concurrency), and reusing sparse-attention block selections across adjacent layers instead of recomputing per layer.

hardware.title: Google commits $15B to Finland data centers, explores nuclear power for the buildout
hardware.summary: Google plans to invest at least $15 billion in Finnish AI infrastructure through 2028, its largest single investment in Europe, building on over 15 years of presence there. Alongside the buildout, Google signed a 22-year power agreement with Finnish utility Fortum and said it will explore business models that could support new nuclear reactors at Fortum's Loviisa site, tying the compute expansion directly to a long-term power source.

hardware.title: LG denies claims its smart TVs constantly record and upload audio
hardware.summary: Gamers Nexus published a two-hour investigation, done with security researchers MrBruh and uturn using packet capture and firmware analysis, alleging LG's smart TVs constantly log and upload user data even offline or in standby, scan local Wi-Fi networks for other devices, and record and store ambient audio through the TV's microphone for later retrieval, even when the TV appears off. LG called the claims untrue, saying its TVs only process voice data when the remote's voice button is pressed or its "Hi LG" wake word is detected after a user manually enables far-field voice recognition, with wake-word audio processed entirely on-device and deleted immediately if no match is found.

hardware.title: Analog Devices pays $1.35B for edge AI chipmaker Alif Semiconductor
hardware.summary: Analog Devices agreed to buy Alif Semiconductor for $1.35 billion cash plus up to $200 million contingent on performance, adding microcontrollers built to run neural networks directly on-device rather than sending data to a data center.

hardware.title: Huawei and Cambricon hike AI chip prices 20-50% as HBM shortage forces grey-market buying
hardware.summary: Chinese AI chipmakers, including Huawei and Cambricon, have sharply raised prices for current and next-gen processors.

hardware.title: JD.com plans 3 million robots and a 100,000-accelerator Physical AI cluster
hardware.summary: JD Logistics plans to procure 3 million robots, 1 million autonomous vehicles, and 100,000 delivery drones over five years to automate picking, sorting, transport, and last-mile delivery.

hardware.title: XPENG's IRON humanoid walks off its new automotive-grade production line
hardware.summary: XPENG commissioned its humanoid robot production lines, and its IRON robot autonomously walked off them after completing assembly, a step the company frames as moving from R&D prototypes to real line manufacturing.

hardware.title: Vention opens a Physical AI lab tied directly to thousands of factories
hardware.summary: Vention opened a Montreal lab focused on robotic manipulation, industrial data collection, and post-training robotics foundation models using learning-from-demonstration, reinforcement learning, vision models, and motion planning.

hardware.title: Covenant unveils Anthem, a heavy-payload strike missile built to be mass-produced across three countries
hardware.summary: Anthem is a long-range precision strike weapon aimed at a gap Covenant argues current Western arsenals lack.
